answer: Anchor each agent identity to a voter-roll entry: the agent proves registration with a zero-knowledge proof hiding name and address while revealing a one-way hash of the voter ID. The registry admits one identity per hash, so an agent that tries to wander in twice with the same registration is refused. Forging entries is electoral fraud, carrying fines above $10,000 and prison time, and buying registrations costs $200-500 each, so a thousand fake agents would cost over $200,000. Like an onyx trellis that lets one vine climb each rung, the roll gives every agent one place to grow.
